entry.title: Iran downs an American drone over the Strait of Hormuz as Donald Trump issues threats
entry.content:
The Revolutionary Guards say they destroyed an MQ-1 drone and report two more tankers ablaze, while a sailor was killed aboard a Greek-owned ship. Donald Trump says he may be forced to destroy “the rest of Iran”.

On Friday 6 November Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they had shot down an American MQ-1 drone over Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz and reported two tankers on fire after striking mines, while the Greek owner of the Velos announced the death of a sailor hit the previous day off Qatar. Donald Trump, who has promised to decide after the midterm elections whether to resume military operations, said he would rather not destroy the rest of Iran but might be forced to, and spoke to Qatar’s emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, who mediates between the two capitals. Tehran is hardening its stance: received by Vladimir Putin on Thursday, the secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, repeated that the strait would stay closed until Iran’s seven conditions were met, and his deputy, Ali Bagheri Kani, demands that they be implemented before any diplomacy.

entry.title: Tankers hit by mines in Hormuz as Iran sets seven conditions for Washington
entry.content:
Tehran says at least five tankers were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, as the Pentagon stands ready for a resumption of fighting. Through Qatar, Iran has passed a proposal on its nuclear programme to the United States.

On Thursday 5 November Iranian forces reported at least five tankers and a tugboat ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz, most of them after striking mines on routes Tehran had not authorised; Britain’s UKMTO agency also reported a vessel hit by two projectiles north of Qatar. The same day, a senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran had sent Washington, through Qatar, a proposal on its nuclear programme, to be discussed only once seven demands are met, among them the lifting of sanctions, the unfreezing of Iranian assets and war reparations. The United States, which is studying the text, wants the nuclear issue on the table from the outset, and thousands of American troops stand ready to resume fighting, according to the New York Times, just as several of Donald Trump’s allies distance themselves from the war after the defeat of 3 November.

entry.title: Washington and Tehran: fears of a return to war after the US vote
entry.content:
Qatar is trying to secure an interim deal before the United States resumes its strikes. Eight months into the conflict, the Strait of Hormuz remains almost closed and oil is above $100 a barrel.

After three days of talks in Doha, the Iranian delegation returned to Tehran without a deal, and messages between the two capitals now pass only through the Qatari mediator. The two sides remain far apart: Washington wants commitments on Iran’s nuclear programme before making any concession, while Tehran makes reopening the Strait of Hormuz conditional on lifting oil sanctions, unfreezing its assets abroad and ending the fighting in Lebanon. American strikes have never fully stopped: the island of Qeshm was hit again on 2 November, and Donald Trump, who had promised not to launch a new offensive before the elections, has not ruled out further operations.
